content: The test image shows a corn ear cross-section (tip-down view) with: white cottony mold in the center/cob area, grayish-white discolored kernels, and pinkish-red coloration between kernels. This points to an ear rot. Top candidates: Fusarium, Ear_rots_Gibberella, Ear_rots_Diplodia.

Key observations from the test image:
- Corn ear viewed from the tip (cross-section)
- White cottony mold concentrated at the center/cob (silk channel entry point)
- Kernels are grayish-white with pinkish-red coloration between and on kernels
- The mold appears to originate from the tip/silk channel area

Comparing to references:
- **Fusarium**: white-pink/salmon scattered mold with starburst on kernels — doesn't match as well
- **Gibberella**: pinkish-white mold at ear TIP progressing from silk channel, pink-red kernel streaking — matches the tip location and pink coloration
- **Diplodia**: white mold starting from BASE of ear, grayish-brown kernels — wrong location for what's seen

The tip-origin location of the white mold + pink/red kernel discoloration strongly aligns with Gibberella ear rot, which infects via the silk channel at the tip.
